newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African budget rollovers, double counts to end.
newsitem.headline: S.African budget rollovers, double counts to end.

text.p: Anomalies in the budget caused by rollovers and the reconstruction and development fund would be removed when government introduced multi-year budgeting next year, Finance Department officials said on Thursday.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said the problem of rollovers, introduced in 1991 to curb the surge of expenditure towards the end of each financial year, would be remedied by the shift towards multi-year budgeting.
"This would allow us to project more clearly what the expenditure and what the capital coverage would be in any single year and so the issue of rollovers would disappear," Manuel said.
State Expenditure director-general Hannes Smit said that of the 12 billion rand not spent in 1995/96, only 8.9 billion rand had been allowed to rollover into 1996/97.
Manuel said the initial phase of multi-year budgeting would be implemented in 1998/99 within the framework of the department's medium-term expenditure plans.
Another anomaly in the budget accounts has been double accounting because of transfers from the reconstruction and development programme (RDP) fund.
"Luckily, this is the last year that we will deal with RDP accounts," Smit said.
This was because the last of the funds would be transferred from the department of finance to the RDP fund, and then from the RDP fund to the relevant departments through the exchequer.
The double count for the RDP fund this year was 4.1 billion rand.
Manuel also said he planned to give more financial responsibility to provinces in his budget which will be delivered on March 12.
"(The budget) will be different from previous budgets because the provinces are being given lump sums in terms of the formula decided by the Financial and Fiscal Commission," Manuel said.
In terms of the new constitution, the provinces are to manage their own expenditure.
"As a step towards that we will see the provinces taking more responsibility in this area," Manuel said.
Special attention was being paid to training provincial finance ministers and their staff to allow them to cope with their finances efficiently, he added.
